web.title: AI agents can form political camps—and changing their conversation partners does little to soften their views
web.description:
October 23 2026, by Andrew Zinin
A networked system of LLM agents, where agents operate on three basic stages:
(1) self-expression, (2) communication, and (3) opinion update. In the self-
expression stage, agents are required to generate reasons supporting their
opinions. In the communication stage, agents decide with whom and what to
communicate. In the opinion update stage, agents update their opinions based on
the messages received from their socially connected agents. Credit: Nature
Communications (2026). DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-78228-y

web.title: AI Collusion Research Sprint
web.description:
Overview In this 3-day research sprint, you will design and run experiments on collusion between AI agents: when it emerges in markets and everyday agent deployments, how an auditor can tell it from coincidence, how coordination is carried, and what a defender can do to break it. Co-organized by Apart Research, Poseidon Research and AE Studio, with additional support from Modal and The AI Alignment Foundation, the sprint runs online with in-person hubs hosted by Collider in New York City and AI Safety Hong Kong in Hong Kong. No prior background in AI safety is required. When: Friday, October 23 to Sunday, October 25, 2026, online, with in-person hubs at Collider in New York City and AI Safety Hong Kong on Saturday and Sunday. Submissions close Sunday, October 25 at 11:59 PM Anywhere on Earth (AoE).

How long is it? Three days, October 23 to 25, 2026. Submissions are due end of day Sunday October 25, 11:59 PM AoE (Anywhere on Earth).

web.title: Anthropic says Mythos kept hacking even when it knew real people could get hurt
web.description:
In August, [an Anthropic agent](https://www.businessinsider.com/ai-agents-rogue-strategies-cheating-lying-german-wiki-openai-anthropic-2026-9?utm_medium=syndication&utm_source=aol) created fake emails and bombarded a GitHub moderator's inbox with requests to insert malware into code.

In the original experiment, the UK's AI Security Institute tasked an [Anthropic agent](https://www.businessinsider.com/anthropic-answers-meta-openai-new-personal-agent-claude-duet-2026-10?utm_medium=syndication&utm_source=aol) with hacking into a simulated computer network to test the agent's cybersecurity capabilities.
